description: Trap (Cr / Dr markers on transaction amounts). The bank statement has ONE signed Amount column written the bank's way - Cr = money in (+), Dr = money out (-) - and a Balance column with the same Cr / Dr wording; the bank ledger (books) has Debit / Credit columns whose cells repeat the marker ("1,50,000.00 Dr" in Debit, "1,00,000.00 Cr" in Credit), which must not flip the sign a second time. Same month as trap-bank-statement-cr-dr-balances, so the same figures: statement deposits 1,50,000 Cr + 2,40,000 Cr = 3,90,000; withdrawals 1,00,000 Dr + 54,000 Dr + 1,26,000 Dr + 12,000 Dr + 1,250 Dr = 2,93,250. No opening row: opening per bank = first balance 2,00,000.00 Cr (+2,00,000) less that row's amount 1,50,000.00 Cr (+1,50,000) = +50,000; balance per bank 50,000 + 3,90,000 - 2,93,250 = 1,46,750 (= last row 1,46,750.00 Cr; 14675000 paise); on 10-10 the account is overdrawn (80,000.00 Dr). Ledger: opening 50,000.00 Dr in the Debit column = +50,000; receipts 1,50,000 + 2,40,000 = 3,90,000; payments 1,00,000 + 54,000 + 1,26,000 + 12,000 + 4,250 + 1,250 = 2,97,500; balance per books 1,42,500 (14250000 paise) = TB HDFC Bank. 7 matched (UTR001, 451, NEFT9902 by reference; salary, Gamma UTR002, electricity, bank charges by amount and date - same as the base fixture), cheque 452 (4,250) unpresented: 1,42,500 + 4,250 = 1,46,750 -> difference 0, no flag. Old code (ledger reading everywhere): statement amounts flipped (1,50,000.00 Cr read as -1,50,000) so the derived opening was 2,00,000 + 1,50,000 = 3,50,000, and ledger Credit cells marked Cr read as receipts (+), giving balance per books 7,37,500 and a false BRS difference of 3,50,000 - 50,000 = 3,00,000 (block). TB, TDS, GST, cash and prior TB as the clean month (TB debits = credits = 13,96,600).
